translation_en: Yahya ibn Yahya informed us: Yazid ibn Zuray‘ informed us, from Ayyub, from Nafi‘, that Ibn ‘Umar used to lease his farms during the Messenger of Allah’s time, the rule of Abu Bakr, ‘Umar, and ‘Uthman, and the early part of Mu‘awiyah’s rule. Toward the end of Mu‘awiyah’s rule, he heard that Rafi‘ ibn Khadij was reporting a prohibition from the Prophet. Ibn ‘Umar went to him, and I was with him, and asked him. He said the Messenger of Allah used to forbid leasing farms. Ibn ‘Umar then stopped leasing them. Whenever asked about it afterward, he would say, “Rafi‘ ibn Khadij claims that the Messenger of Allah forbade it.”

Abu al-Rabi‘ and Abu Kamil narrated to us: Hammad narrated to us; and ‘Ali ibn Hujr narrated to me: Isma‘il narrated to us. Both reported from Ayyub with this chain and a report like it. Ibn ‘Ulayyah’s report adds: Ibn ‘Umar stopped afterward and no longer leased them.

Ibn Numayr narrated to us: my father narrated to us: ‘Ubayd Allah narrated to us, from Nafi‘, who said: I went with Ibn ‘Umar to Rafi‘ ibn Khadij at al-Balat. He told him that the Messenger of Allah forbade leasing farms.

Ibn Abi Khalaf and Hajjaj ibn al-Sha‘ir narrated to me: Zakariyya ibn ‘Adi informed us: ‘Ubayd Allah ibn ‘Amr informed us, from Zayd, from al-Hakam, from Nafi‘, from Ibn ‘Umar, that he went to Rafi‘ and mentioned this report from the Prophet.

Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna narrated to us: Husayn, Ibn Hasan ibn Yasar, narrated to us: Ibn ‘Awn narrated to us, from Nafi‘, that Ibn ‘Umar used to rent out land. He was then informed about a report from Rafi‘ ibn Khadij, so he took me with him to Rafi‘. Rafi‘ mentioned from some of his paternal uncles that the Prophet forbade leasing land. Ibn ‘Umar then stopped renting it.
Muhammad ibn Hatim narrated it to me: Yazid ibn Harun narrated to us: Ibn ‘Awn narrated to us, with this chain, saying that Rafi‘ reported it from some of his paternal uncles, from the Prophet.

‘Abd al-Malik ibn Shu‘ayb ibn al-Layth ibn Sa‘d narrated to me: my father narrated to me, from my grandfather: ‘Uqayl ibn Khalid narrated to me, from Ibn Shihab, who said: Salim ibn ‘Abd Allah informed me that ‘Abd Allah ibn ‘Umar used to lease his lands until he heard that Rafi‘ ibn Khadij al-Ansari forbade leasing land. ‘Abd Allah met him and asked, “Ibn Khadij, what do you report from the Messenger of Allah about leasing land?” Rafi‘ said, “I heard my two paternal uncles, both of whom had fought at Badr, tell the people of the household that the Messenger of Allah forbade leasing land.” ‘Abd Allah said, “I knew during the Messenger of Allah’s time that land was leased,” but then feared the Messenger might have instituted something of which he was unaware, so he stopped leasing land.

Yahya ibn Yahya said: I recited to Malik, from Rabi‘ah ibn Abi ‘Abd al-Rahman, from Hanzalah ibn Qays, that he asked Rafi‘ ibn Khadij about leasing land. Rafi‘ said the Messenger of Allah forbade leasing land. I asked, “What about payment in gold and silver?” He said, “There is no harm in that.”

Ishaq informed us: ‘Isa ibn Yunus narrated to us: al-Awza‘i narrated to us, from Rabi‘ah ibn Abi ‘Abd al-Rahman, who narrated to me: Hanzalah ibn Qays al-Ansari said: I asked Rafi‘ ibn Khadij about leasing land for gold or silver. He said, “There is no harm in that. In the Prophet’s time people leased land for irrigation channels, the banks of streams, and parts of the crops. Sometimes one portion yielded while another did not, or one was spared while another failed, and that was all the people had as rent. For that reason it was prohibited. But there is no harm in a known, guaranteed payment.”

‘Amr al-Naqid narrated to us: Sufyan ibn ‘Uyaynah narrated to us, from Yahya ibn Sa‘id, from Hanzalah al-Zuraqi, who heard Rafi‘ ibn Khadij say: We were among the Ansar with the most fields. We leased land on the condition that this portion would be ours and that portion theirs; sometimes one yielded and the other did not. He forbade us from doing that, but he did not forbid payment in silver.
Abu al-Rabi‘ narrated to us: Hammad narrated to us; and Ibn al-Muthanna narrated to us: Yazid ibn Harun narrated to us. Both reported from Yahya ibn Sa‘id with this chain and a report like it.

‘Ali ibn Hujr al-Sa‘di and Ya‘qub ibn Ibrahim narrated to me: Isma‘il, Ibn ‘Ulayyah, narrated to us, from Ayyub, from Ya‘la ibn Hakim, from Sulayman ibn Yasar, from Rafi‘ ibn Khadij, who said: We practiced sharecropping in the Messenger of Allah’s time, renting land for a third, a fourth, or a specified amount of food. One day a man from my paternal uncles came and said, “The Messenger of Allah forbade something that benefited us, but obedience to Allah and His Messenger benefits us more. He forbade us to lease land for a third, a fourth, or a specified amount of food. He ordered the landowner to cultivate it or have it cultivated, and disliked renting it or anything else in exchange.”

Yahya ibn Yahya narrated it to us: Hammad ibn Zayd narrated to us, from Ayyub, who said: Ya‘la ibn Hakim wrote to me: I heard Sulayman ibn Yasar narrate from Rafi‘ ibn Khadij that they practiced sharecropping, leasing land for a third or a fourth. Then he mentioned a report like Ibn ‘Ulayyah’s.

Yahya ibn Habib narrated to us: Khalid ibn al-Harith narrated to us; ‘Amr ibn ‘Ali narrated to us: ‘Abd al-A‘la narrated to us; and Ishaq ibn Ibrahim informed us: ‘Abdah narrated to us. All reported from Ibn Abi ‘Arubah, from Ya‘la ibn Hakim, with this chain and a report like it.

Abu al-Tahir informed me: Ibn Wahb informed us: Jarir ibn Hazim informed me, from Ya‘la ibn Hakim, with this chain from Rafi‘ ibn Khadij, from the Prophet, without saying that it came from some of his paternal uncles.

Ishaq ibn Mansur informed me: Abu Mushir informed us: Yahya ibn Hamzah narrated to me: Abu ‘Amr al-Awza‘i narrated to me, from Abu al-Najashi, the client of Rafi‘ ibn Khadij, from Rafi‘, that his uncle Zuhayr ibn Rafi‘ came to him and said: “The Messenger of Allah forbade something that had been useful to us.” I said, “Whatever the Messenger of Allah said is true.” He said: The Prophet asked, “What do you do with your fields?” I said, “We lease them for spring produce or for measures of dates or barley.” He said: “Do not do that. Cultivate them yourselves, let others cultivate them, or leave them.”

Muhammad ibn Hatim narrated to us: ‘Abd al-Rahman ibn Mahdi narrated to us, from ‘Ikrimah ibn ‘Ammar, from Abu al-Najashi, from Rafi‘, from the Prophet, with this report, but he did not mention his uncle Zuhayr.

Yahya ibn Yahya informed us: ‘Abd al-Wahid ibn Ziyad narrated to us; Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah narrated to us: ‘Ali ibn Mushir narrated to us. Both reported from al-Shaybani, from ‘Abd Allah ibn al-Sa’ib, who said: I asked ‘Abd Allah ibn Ma‘qil about sharecropping. He said: Thabit ibn al-Dahhak informed me that the Messenger of Allah forbade sharecropping. Ibn Abi Shaybah’s narration says simply, “He forbade it.” It says, “I asked Ibn Ma‘qil,” without naming ‘Abd Allah.

Ishaq ibn Mansur informed us: Yahya ibn Hammad informed us: Abu ‘Awanah informed us, from Sulayman al-Shaybani, from ‘Abd Allah ibn al-Sa’ib, who said: We visited ‘Abd Allah ibn Ma‘qil and asked him about sharecropping. He said: Thabit claimed that the Messenger of Allah forbade sharecropping and ordered leasing, saying, “There is no harm in that.”

Yahya ibn Yahya informed us: Hammad ibn Zayd narrated to us, from ‘Amr, that Mujahid said to Tawus: “Come with us to Ibn Rafi‘ ibn Khadij and hear the hadith from his father, from the Prophet.” He rebuked him and said, “By Allah, if I knew the Messenger of Allah forbade it, I would not do it. But someone more knowledgeable about it than they—meaning Ibn ‘Abbas—told me that the Messenger of Allah said: ‘For a man to grant his land to his brother is better for him than to take a specified rent for it.’”

Ibn Abi ‘Umar narrated to us: Sufyan narrated to us, from ‘Amr; and Ibn Tawus reported from Tawus, who used to practice mukhabarah. ‘Amr said: I told him, “Abu ‘Abd al-Rahman, if only you stopped this mukhabarah, since they claim the Prophet forbade it.” He replied, “O ‘Amr, the most knowledgeable of them, meaning Ibn ‘Abbas, informed me that the Prophet did not forbid it. He only said: ‘For one of you to grant his land to his brother is better than taking a specified rent for it.’”

Ibn Abi ‘Umar narrated to us: al-Thaqafi narrated to us, from Ayyub; Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah and Ishaq ibn Ibrahim both reported from Waki‘, from Sufyan; Muhammad ibn Rumh reported from al-Layth, from Ibn Jurayj; and ‘Ali ibn Hujr narrated to me: al-Fadl ibn Musa narrated to us, from Sharik, from Shu‘bah. All reported from ‘Amr ibn Dinar, from Tawus, from Ibn ‘Abbas, from the Prophet, with a report like theirs.

‘Abd ibn Humayd and Muhammad ibn Rafi‘ narrated to me. ‘Abd said: He informed us; Ibn Rafi‘ said: ‘Abd al-Razzaq informed us: Ma‘mar informed us, from Ibn Tawus, from his father, from Ibn ‘Abbas, that the Prophet said: “For one of you to grant his land to his brother is better than taking such-and-such”—a specified amount. Ibn ‘Abbas said: It is al-haql, called muhaqalah in the language of the Ansar.

‘Abd Allah ibn ‘Abd al-Rahman al-Darimi informed us: ‘Abd Allah ibn Ja‘far al-Raqqi narrated to us: ‘Ubayd Allah ibn ‘Amr narrated to us, from Zayd ibn Abi Unaysah, from ‘Abd al-Malik Abu Zayd, from Tawus, from Ibn ‘Abbas, from the Prophet, who said: “If someone has land, it is better for him to grant it to his brother.”

Ahmad ibn Hanbal and Zuhayr ibn Harb narrated to us—and the wording is Zuhayr’s. They said: Yahya, al-Qattan, narrated to us, from ‘Ubayd Allah, who informed me, from Nafi‘, from Ibn ‘Umar, that the Messenger of Allah made an agreement with the people of Khaybar for half of its fruit or crops.

‘Ali ibn Hujr al-Sa‘di narrated to me: ‘Ali, Ibn Mushir, narrated to us: ‘Ubayd Allah informed us, from Nafi‘, from Ibn ‘Umar, who said: The Messenger of Allah gave Khaybar to its people for half of its fruit or crops. Each year he gave his wives one hundred wasqs: eighty wasqs of dates and twenty of barley. When ‘Umar took charge, he divided Khaybar and offered the Prophet’s wives either land and water or a guaranteed amount of produce each year. They differed: some chose the land and water, while others chose the annual produce. ‘Aishah and Hafsah were among those who chose land and water.

Ibn Numayr narrated to us: my father narrated to us: ‘Ubayd Allah narrated to us: Nafi‘ narrated to me, from ‘Abd Allah ibn ‘Umar, that the Messenger of Allah made an agreement with the people of Khaybar for half of its crops or fruit. The narrator related the hadith like ‘Ali ibn Mushir’s, but omitted the statement that ‘Aishah and Hafsah chose land and water. It says he offered the Prophet’s wives land, without mentioning water.

Abu al-Tahir narrated to me: ‘Abd Allah ibn Wahb narrated to us: Usamah ibn Zayd al-Laythi informed me, from Nafi‘, from ‘Abd Allah ibn ‘Umar, who said: When Khaybar was conquered, its Jews asked the Messenger of Allah to let them remain there in exchange for working the land for half of its fruit and crops. He said: “I will let you remain on that basis as long as we wish.” Then he related a report like Ibn Numayr’s and Ibn Mushir’s from ‘Ubayd Allah, adding that the produce was divided into shares from half of Khaybar and the Messenger of Allah took one fifth.

Ibn Rumh informed us: al-Layth informed us, from Muhammad ibn ‘Abd al-Rahman, from Nafi‘, from ‘Abd Allah ibn ‘Umar, from the Messenger of Allah, that he gave the Jews of Khaybar its date palms and land to work with their own resources, and the Messenger of Allah was to receive half its fruit.

Muhammad ibn Rafi‘ and Ishaq ibn Mansur narrated to me—and the wording is Ibn Rafi‘’s. They said: ‘Abd al-Razzaq narrated to us: Ibn Jurayj informed us: Musa ibn ‘Uqbah narrated to me, from Nafi‘, from Ibn ‘Umar, that ‘Umar ibn al-Khattab expelled the Jews and Christians from the land of the Hijaz. When the Messenger of Allah prevailed at Khaybar, he wanted to expel its Jews, since the land belonged to Allah, His Messenger, and the Muslims. The Jews asked him to let them remain and work it, receiving half its produce. He said, “We will let you remain on that basis as long as we wish.” They remained there until ‘Umar expelled them to Tayma’ and Ariha’.
